_what_this_is: The shelves teachers have published: which titles from the approved catalogue each course is actually teaching, when in the year, and how students get the text. Maintained by hand, once a year. The ELA Reference Library reads this file at build time and renders the Teacher Bookshelves view from it.
_how_a_new_year_works: Start a new file. Change school_year, empty the classrooms list, and keep last year's file so the previous year stays readable. Nothing here expires on its own.
_how_to_add_a_teacher: Add one object to classrooms below, per course. A teacher with three courses is three objects with the same teacher name. Teachers can produce their own block from the My Classroom tab in the Reference Library and send it to you; paste it in rather than retyping.

_fields.teacher: required, free text, exactly as it should appear on the shelf
_fields.course: required, free text, e.g. English III
_fields.subject: optional, defaults to ELA
_fields.grade: required, K through 12, as a string
_fields.level: blank, Honors or AP. Blank means Standard.
_fields.delivery: Live or On-Demand. Defaults to Live.
_fields.period: class period for a Live course, or null. Ignored for On-Demand.
_fields.titles: list of titles taught. Each entry is either a bare catalogue id or an object, see _title_entries. Ids come from library.json. An id that does not exist FAILS THE BUILD rather than rendering a blank line.

_title_entries._two_forms: A bare id string still works and always will: the first year of shelves was written that way. It means 'taught, quarter and access not stated'. Use the object form to say more.

_object.quarter: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, or blank. Blank is not an error: it means the teacher has not placed it yet, and the shelf groups those under 'Not yet placed in a quarter' rather than guessing Q1.
_object.access: purchase = the student buys a copy. provided = Optima provides the text or an excerpt in class. Blank means nobody has said, which is deliberately different from either answer.

_title_entries._note_on_access: This is separate from the Free/Similar/Buy pill. That pill says what the TEXT is under copyright. access says what THIS teacher does about it: a public-domain text can still be handed out in class, and an in-copyright one can still be a student purchase.
